topology_reasoning.evidence: The black material consists of two horizontally through-going, equal-width waveguides. Their centerlines approach symmetrically from a wide separation, remain closest around the horizontal midpoint, then mirror-diverge. There are no branches, tapers to a single guide, rings, or crossings.
topology_reasoning.operation: Evanescent coupling transfers power between the guides while their separation is small; the accumulated coupling is controlled primarily by the close-proximity interaction length and gap.
topology_reasoning.geometry_model: Two mirrored smooth sampled centerlines made with gf.Path and variable-width extrusion. The endpoints are separated by about 2.35 um center-to-center; the midpoint separation is about 0.96 um. The apparent guide width is about 0.65 um, with a shallow central widening.

iterations.change_made: Initial primitives-only reconstruction: two mirrored cosine-squared gf.Path S-bends, piecewise-extruded with the shallow calibrated central width increase. The GDS is flattened only at write time so the external area measurer sees its primitive-built geometry. The residual is a shape-profile mismatch, but the phase threshold was reached on the first valid comparison.

knob_response.note: The generic verifier is an MZI delta-length contract: it correctly observes that a symmetric directional coupler changes neither differential arm length nor total material area by width times transfer_length. It therefore reports passes=false despite the transfer-length profile changing. No artificial MZI arm/dummy geometry was added.
